subject: Specifying prior distribution for more than 1 item parameters at a time

messages.author: 84aac2580b195c68
messages.subject: Specifying prior distribution for more than 1 item parameters at a time
parts:
Hello Phil and everyone,


During calibration if you want to specify the prior distribution, you can specify by following syntax



model <- mirt.model('F = 1-5
                     PRIOR = (1-5, a1, lnorm, 1, 0.3)')


mod1.3PL.norm2 <- mirt(data,model, itemtype = '3PL')


I need to specify more than one parameters' prior distribution simultaneously.

for e.g. I want to specify a1's prior distribution as log-normal with mean 1 and standard deviation 0.3, d's prior distribution as normal with mean=0 and standard deviation= 1 and g's prior distribution as a normal distribution with a mean of .20 and a
standard deviation of 0.03.

How can I do that?


Regards,

Irshad

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Specifying prior distribution for more than 1 item parameters at a time
parts:
Priors, like constraints, can be specified by separating the syntax arguments with a comma. So this would do it:

model <- mirt.model('F = 1-5,
                                 PRIOR = (1-5, a1, lnorm, .2, .2), (1-5, d, norm, 0, 1), (1-5, g, norm, -1.386294, .2)

Note that the g parameter is a normal/Gaussian prior since internally they are transformed to logit values, log(g/(1-g)), for better numerical stability, so priors should also follow this form too. Here the mean value is determined by checking qlogis(.2) = -1.386294. Cheers.

Phil
